ORIGINAL ISSUE: GR4J runs on a 101,033 km² catchment and returns NSE -19.6
## Why this matters

The Model tab offers "Calibrate GR4J" on every gauge, including ones where the method cannot work.

On Colorado Rv at Austin (101,033 km²) it runs and returns KGE 0.462 calibration / -5.811 validation, NSE -0.075 / -19.634, PBIAS 5.6 % / 591.9 %. The caveat printed underneath is correct and honest ("forcing at the gauge point, not catchment-averaged, so wet mountainous catchments will under-run"), but by then the table of numbers is already on screen. Point forcing over 101,033 km² was never going to work, and `panel-station.js:277` looks the area up before the solver starts, so the app knows.

Someone arriving from a launch post and picking the most famous gauge they can name currently gets NSE -19.6 as their first impression of the modelling.

Timing is the second half. The copy at `index.html:220` says "Runs in your browser in a few seconds". The solver is genuinely fast (820 simulations in 2.0 s), but the whole click took 110 s: the catchment lookup, then 40 years of Open-Meteo hourly-to-daily forcing. For 100 of those seconds the panel says "Looking up the catchment area…" against copy promising seconds.

## What to change

Gate on area, after the lookup at `panel-station.js:277` and before the forcing fetch:

```js
const AREA_WARN_KM2 = 10_000;
if (area.area > AREA_WARN_KM2) {
  // render an inline confirm rather than proceeding
  say(`This catchment is ${fmt(area.area)} km². The forcing is taken at the gauge point, not averaged over
       the catchment, so a basin this size will not calibrate meaningfully. Run it anyway?`, "warn");
  // wait for an explicit click before continuing
}
```

Keep it a warning with an opt-in rather than a hard block: someone comparing methods may well want the bad fit, and it is their call.

The threshold is a judgement rather than a constant from anywhere; 10,000 km² is where point forcing stops being arguable. Worth stating in the text so the reader can disagree with it.

For the copy, describe what is actually slow:

> Fits the four-parameter GR4J model to this record with ERA5-Land/ERA5 rainfall and FAO-56 ET0 at the gauge (Open-Meteo). Downloading the forcing takes a minute or two; the fit itself takes a few seconds.

And the progress line should name the step it is on, so "Downloading 40 years of forcing…" replaces a silent stretch under "Looking up the catchment area…".

## Steps

1. Add the area gate with an explicit opt-in, after the area lookup.
2. Split the progress messages so each long step names itself.
3. Rewrite the description at `index.html:220`.
4. Test the gate at the boundary, both sides.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A catchment above the threshold warns and waits for an explicit click
- [ ] The warning names the area and why point forcing fails at that size
- [ ] Progress text matches the step actually running
- [ ] The description no longer promises seconds for the whole click

### Issues Fixed
1. **Catchment Area Gate in GR4J Calibration**: Added an area threshold check (`const AREA_WARN_KM2 = 10_000;`) in `explorer/src/panel-station.js` after fetching the station area. 2. **Progress Messaging**: Split and refined the progress steps so each long operation (`Looking up the catchment area…`, `Downloading 40 years of forcing…`, etc.) explicitly names the task currently running.
3. **Description Copy Update**: Updated the model tab description copy in `explorer/src/index.html` (around line 220) to clarify that downloading forcing data takes a minute or two while the fit itself takes a few seconds.
